title_original: In Santa Fe, One Hundred Photographers and Forty-Five Reviewers
excerpt_original: From October 23 to 26, Santa Fe becomes a meeting place for photographers and the people who can publish, exhibit or acquire their work. The 25th Review Santa Fe Photo Symposium, organised by CENTER, schedules nearly 1,000 one-on-one portfolio reviews. One evening, the Portfolio…

blocks.text: Picture a large pavilion, strings of bare bulbs hanging from the ceiling, and long tables covered in white cloth. On them, prints are laid out edge to edge, wooden boxes stand open, and books are propped up like small altars. Behind each table, a photographer waits. In front, visitors lean in, turn a page, ask a question. A reviewer from a major publication stops, then stays. This is the Portfolio Walk, the public face of Review Santa Fe. Each year, the evening draws crowds. CENTER says more than 1,000 people can pass through in a single night.

Review Santa Fe is first of all a working conference. One hundred photographers, selected by an independent committee, travel to New Mexico with a project they hope will find a wider audience. There, they sit down with the people who can help it do so.

This year, CENTER welcomes 19 editors, including representatives of National Geographic , The New York Times , Oxford American and NPR. They are joined by 10 museum curators, 7 book publishers and 9 gallery representatives. That makes 45 reviewers, who spend the weekend looking at work and deciding which of it deserves to travel further. The result is nearly 1,000 one-on-one meetings in four days.

Participation is by application. A selection committee of three industry professionals ranks the submitted projects, and invited photographers then pay a fee for their package of reviews. CENTER says scholarships and payment plans are available.

The format reflects CENTER’s own history. Founded in 1994, the Santa Fe non-profit supports socially and environmentally engaged lens-based projects through education, funding and partnerships. Review Santa Fe is its largest event of the year.

The weekend opens on October 23 at CENTER Gallery with The Conditions of Seeing , an exhibition of the 2026 award and grant recipients: Marcus DeSieno, Anna Mia Davidson, Leonard Suryajaya, Peter Teh, Ville Varumo and Volodymyr Voznyy.

The show gathers landscape, portraiture, staged scenes, diary-like image-making and socially engaged practice. What links them is a question: under what conditions do people, places and selves become visible? Their work looks at how seeing is shaped by political systems, inherited histories, environmental change, cultural assumptions, relationships, memory and care.

On the morning of October 25, Marcus DeSieno, a Project Launch Grant recipient, presents Geography of Disappearance: Migrant Deaths on the US/Mexico Border . The United Nations has described the border as the deadliest land crossing in the world. DeSieno photographs along it, going to the exact places where the bodies of unknown migrants were found. He locates them using autopsy reports and data collected by humanitarian organisations and by local and state police. The photographs, he writes in his project statement, serve “as a space for somber remembrance of the deceased.”

Most of the public programme is free. The Portfolio Walk takes place on October 24 and lets visitors speak directly with the hundred photographers. The work covers a wide range of contemporary photography on social, environmental and political subjects. It can be previewed beforehand on the Review Santa Fe Listing website. On October 26, a panel with the reviewers, moderated by Thomas Werner, closes the weekend with a discussion of how photographic projects get published and exhibited.
Online and in-person events are both offered this year.

The Review Santa Fe Photo Symposium takes place from October 23 to 26, 2026, in Santa Fe, New Mexico (USA). The full programme is on CENTER’s website , and the work of the hundred photographers can be previewed on the Review Santa Fe Listing . Applications for the 2026 edition closed on February 28, and the next call for entry opens in January 2027 on CENTER’s application page .
